messages.subject: [statnet_help] Errors with "simulate" on our Linux machine
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Errors with "simulate" on our Linux machine
messages.body_plain:
Hello and happy new year,
I've got the statnet version with the 2.4-0 binary release of latentnet at home and at work. It's fine on my PC (Windows XP) but I'm not able to run "simulate" on my Linux machine at work. There is a different complaint depending on the arguments passed. After my models failed, I tried an example from the article published in JSS 24(9). Here is the failure with that standard example, using various arguments for "simulate". Any clues? It is R 2.11.1.

Thanks
Jeremy

Institute for Transport Systems and Planning, ETH Zurich
http://www.ivt.ethz.ch/people/jhackney

> fmh<-faux.magnolia.high
> plot(fmh)
> model1<-ergm(fmh~edges+nodematch("Grade")+nodematch("Race")+nodematch("Sex"))
> sim1<-simulate(model1)
Error in ans[test & !nas] <- rep(yes, length.out = length(ans))[test &? :
? replacement has length zero

Starting 1 MCMC iteration of? steps.
Error in ans[test & !nas] <- rep(yes, length.out = length(ans))[test &? :
? replacement has length zero

? replacement has length zero

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Estimating alpha with "large" network & running out of RAM with MCMC
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Estimating alpha with "large" network & running out of RAM with MCMC
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I am trying to model the following network but I am running out of memory very 
quickly:

> net 
 Network attributes:
  vertices = 2391 
  directed = FALSE 
  hyper = FALSE 
  loops = FALSE 
  multiple = FALSE 
  bipartite = FALSE 
  total edges= 2170 
    missing edges= 0 
    non-missing edges= 2170 


I am using a R 64 bit installation on a Windows 7 64 bit with 4Gb of RAM. After 
reading the documentation on gwdsp and MCMC estimation, I understand it may take 
a lot of space in memory which may explain this. In [1], David recommanded using 
fixed=TRUE, but I would need a good approximation for alpha. What would be the 
recommanded approach in this case?

regards,

Ben

> big.enough <- 2391 * 2390*4
> summary(model1<-ergm(net ~ 
+      gwdsp(1,fixed=FALSE)
+          
,MCMCsamplesize=1000),control=control.ergm(maxNumDyadTypes=big.enough)) 

Iteration 1 of at most 3 with parameter: 
      gwdsp gwdsp.alpha 
  -2.824872    1.000000 
the log-likelihood improved by 19.70 
Iteration 2 of at most 3 with parameter: 
      gwdsp gwdsp.alpha 
  -2.797609    1.126067 
the log-likelihood improved by 19.87 
Iteration 3 of at most 3 with parameter: 
      gwdsp gwdsp.alpha 
  -2.764455    1.320654 
the log-likelihood improved by 18.66 
Error: cannot allocate vector of size 479.4 Mb
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In attributes(.Data) <- c(attributes(.Data), attrib) :
  Reached total allocation of 4022Mb: see help(memory.size)
2: In attributes(.Data) <- c(attributes(.Data), attrib) :
  Reached total allocation of 4022Mb: see help(memory.size)
3: In attributes(.Data) <- c(attributes(.Data), attrib) :
  Reached total allocation of 4022Mb: see help(memory.size)
4: In attributes(.Data) <- c(attributes(.Data), attrib) :
  Reached total allocation of 4022Mb: see help(memory.size)

messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Estimating alpha with "large" network & running out of RAM with MCMC
messages.body_plain:
In a nutshell, networks this size are simply way too large to try to  
fit curved EF parameters currently.  This is due to the memory  
requirements (gwdsp with fixed=FALSE requires a huge amount of memory,  
unlike when fixed=TRUE).  Try several different values of alpha in the  
range (say) 0 to 1, then look at the estimated likelihoods and go with  
the value that gives the largest estimated likelihood.  If the  
estimated likelihoods are all pretty close, it probably doesn't matter  
much which alpha you choose since the likelihood estimates themselves  
are subject to MCMC error.

Dave

messages.subject: [statnet_help] network v1.6 released
messages.body_plain:
Greetings, all.  This is a quick note to let you know that network v1.6 
is now on CRAN.  This is a minor bugfix release, but resolves two 
annoying issues: the plot.network bug in which edge colors failed if 
specified by a single character string that was not in reference to an 
edge attribute, and the "spooky action at a distance" bug in which 
changing a network object could sometimes modify another object from 
which it had been copied.*

Thanks as always to those who submitted fixes or bug reports -- props 
are given in the ChangeLog.

Enjoy,

-Carter

* The latter is due to what I impertinently regard as a flaw in R's lazy 
evaluation system, coupled with a ban on overloading certain operators 
that were used to avoid the problem in older versions of R.  We now use 
a different workaround.
